about: Rad Law Firm works from Dallas, publishes a fee statement, a free consultation and home or hospital appointments around the clock, and answers in Spanish.

Its Google listing took a manual check to attach: the firm publishes a login name rather than its own name in its structured data, so a search by that name returned four other Dallas practices. It names no attorney on the pages we could reach.

google.source: Google Business Profile via Places API. 2 listings, counts summed and rating weighted by count

G1.evidence: Texas does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

G2.evidence: Texas does not publish a disciplinary register we can query.

G3.evidence: 2 physical locations verified on Google Business Profile. We read the Active Franchise Taxpayers (data.texas.gov 9cir-efmm), published as open data by the Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts, which carries the Secretary of State file number, charter date and status and could not identify this firm in it: 1 entity name(s) contain the firm's name and none of them agrees on both the name and the city. A miss there is not evidence that the firm is unregistered, so this gate is unresolved rather than failed. The franchise tax does not reach a sole proprietorship or a general partnership, so this register can confirm an entity and cannot rule one out.

G5.evidence: Site has served over HTTPS, a working phone number published, 1 named attorney published.
G5.source: Public crawl of the firm's own site

G6.evidence: 551 public client reviews across 2 Google listings, above the 10 minimum, and the firm's domain has been registered since 2001-09-13, so it has been operating for more than a year
G6.source: Google Places API and the domain's registration date over RDAP
